title: FIFA World Cup
summary: This document is a comprehensive overview of the FIFA World Cup, the international association football competition for senior men's national teams. The document begins by introducing the tournament's prestige, viewership figures, its quadrennial schedule since 1930 (excluding 1942 and 1946 due to World War II), the current 48-team format, and the list of past champions, with Brazil leading with five titles. It then traces the tournament's history, covering early international competitions such as Olympic football and the Sir Thomas Lipton Trophy, the inaugural 1930 World Cup in Uruguay, pre- and post-World War II tournaments, expansions from 16 to 24, 32, and eventually 48 teams, the 2015 FIFA corruption case, and a proposed biennial World Cup. The document also describes other FIFA tournaments, including the Women's World Cup and youth competitions. Additional sections detail the history of the trophy (the Jules Rimet Trophy and the current FIFA World Cup Trophy), the qualification and final tournament formats, the host nation selection process and notable hosting performances, broadcasting history and promotional elements such as mascots, official match balls, songs, and sticker albums, and the tournament's significant economic impact on host nations and financial markets. The document concludes with tournament results and team performances by confederation, records and statistics (including top goalscorers like Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi), and post-tournament awards such as the Golden Ball, Golden Boot, and Golden Glove.
